anya: Quick share — finished the GPTQ bake for Llama2-13b / Mistral-7b / Qwen-7b this morning. TL;DR: Mistral has the smallest accuracy delta, Qwen shows instruction-following drift with default GPTQ config. Posting the condensed eval dump below.

sam: Nice, thanks! can you paste the metrics?

anya: Yep — asked eval-bot to collate.

eval-bot: ```
# condensed eval (baseline FP32 vs GPTQ-8bit)
model        | suite    | FP32  | GPTQ  | delta  | latency_p50_ms | gpu_mem_mb
-------------------------------------------------------------------
Llama2-13b   | MMLU     | 52.1% | 49.3% | -2.8pt |  210           | 16384
Mistral-7b   | MMLU     | 48.6% | 47.9% | -0.7pt |  160           | 12288
Qwen-7b      | MMLU     | 50.0% | 45.2% | -4.8pt |  180           | 13500

Llama2-13b   | HF-Instruction | 75.2% | 72.1% | -3.1pt | 220    | 16384
Mistral-7b   | HF-Instruction | 68.9% | 68.4% | -0.5pt | 170    | 12288
Qwen-7b      | HF-Instruction | 79.5% | 71.0% | -8.5pt | 185   | 13500
```

anya: Note the big hit on Qwen for instruction-following (HF-Instruction). MMLU is also worse but less dramatic for Mistral.

jin: Did you use the same GPTQ recipes across all three? or per-model tuning?

anya: Started with a single baseline GPTQ-8bit pass (per-channel, block=128, act-order default), then one tuned run where we adjusted per-channel scale clipping and outlier handling for Mistral/Qwen. The table above is the baseline single-pass.

sam: Any AWQ runs to compare? AWQ tends to be friendlier for Qwen from prior experiments.

anya: ran AWQ-4bit on Qwen-7b and Llama2-13b quick checks. Short summary: AWQ preserved instruction scores better on Qwen (HF-Instruction delta ~ -2.1pt) but increased perplexity on some math tasks. Mistral didn't benefit much from AWQ vs GPTQ.

bakebot: Uploaded raw artifacts to s3://redwood-bakes/gptq/3290012345/ (models + logs + evals).

tara: Can you paste the command + key config used for the baseline GPTQ pass? we should reproduce.

anya: sure — baseline command:
```bash
./scripts/run_gptq.sh \
  --model $MODEL_PATH \
  --out /tmp/gptq_out \
  --bits 8 \
  --per-channel True \
  --block-size 128 \
  --act-order default \
  --clip-scale 2.5
```

anya: and example tweak we tried for Qwen: set --clip-scale 1.8 and --outlier-threshold 3.5 which reduced tail quant error but needed retraining of calibration set.

jin: Interesting on clip-scale. Did you check KV-cache alignment regressions? Qwen's architecture seems sensitive to KV scaling mismatches.

anya: Yup — we ran a KV-alignment smoke test (chat trace replay) and saw small token-wise drift for Qwen leading to early-stop divergence in long-turn chats. Mistral and Llama were stable.

sam: For deployment, what's the recommendation? hold Qwen-GPTQ for now on chat-critical routes?

anya: Recommendation:
- Mistral-7b: GPTQ-8 baseline OK for prod, enable aggressive batching and KV caching. Canary on 10% traffic.
- Llama2-13b: GPTQ-8 okay for retrieval/semantic tasks; for instruction-heavy paths use AWQ or tuned GPTQ.
- Qwen-7b: Do NOT roll GPTQ-8 to instruction/chat paths without AWQ/tuning + expanded calibration set (include multi-turn chat). Use GPTQ on read-only embedding/classification routes only.

tara: sounds reasonable. can we quantify expected perf gains?

anya: Quick numbers from the runs: GPTQ-8 reduces GPU mem by ~20-25% vs FP32 and latency down ~15-25% depending on model and batch. AWQ-4 can further reduce mem but with mixed accuracy tradeoffs.

sam: Action items?

anya: proposed:
1) sam: run AWQ on Qwen-7b with multi-turn calibration set (I'll share prompts) — TAG by EOD+2.
2) jin: add KV-alignment unit test to bake CI for Qwen models (small chat replay).
3) tara: start 10% canary for Mistral-GPTQ-8 on sandbox stage next week.

jin: I'll PR the KV test today.

sam: I'll start AWQ runs tomorrow morning and post logs.

anya: Thanks — leaving more details and sample prompts in the s3 bucket. ping me for access. :thumbsup:
